output.summary: Bounded screen run 2026-10-19 on priority and applicability only. Correctness was not rechecked. No publication I located states the target results: LS(p,p-2), LS(p,p-3) or LS(p,p-4), the reduction LS-II', or the BASE1 E2/E3 classification. Not finding a source does not show novelty. Calibration by claim: (1) LS(p,p-2) appears to follow in about 10 lines from EGZ plus the classical inverse theorems for lengths 2n-2 (Yuster-Peterson; Bialostocki-Dierker) and 2n-3 (Ordaz-Flores, re-derived in Savchev-Chen 2008 Sec. 4). The argument works for every prime p>=5 and needs none of CF, RED, DGM-p, LS-II' or index-one [INFERENCE; derivation in theorem_comparison; unreviewed]. (2) LS(p,p-3) for p>=11 and LS(p,p-4) for p>=13: priority unknown. Steps (B) and (C) of Proposition I-small are exactly Savchev-Chen 2007 Thm 8 and Prop 5 (applied in C_p). The EGZ split plus SC2008 Thm 5 gives a classical normal form for Y-A exactly when p>4e-4, a range that contains both stated p-ranges. I did not carry out the remaining casework (translations and boundary multiplicities). This is a plausible specialist delta and may well be routine. (3) BASE1 Theorem: Zeng-Yuan 2011 applies directly to T, which has length 2p+2 and is a product of two atoms (by D(C_2p)=2p and BASE1 S1-S2). Their result is that zero-sum sequences of length >=2*floor(n/2)+2 that are products of at most two atoms have coefficients summing to 2n with respect to some g; I read only the zbMATH summary. The E2/E3 analysis then becomes an elementary counting argument of about 12 lines (given below). So the Theorem looks corollary-level given ZY2011 [INFERENCE], and this route also avoids importing S1-sharp. BASE1+ still needs the lane's own accepted SLZ3. (4) LS-II' is internal scaffolding for the lane, and I expect no literature analogue. Tools for the remaining LS case (I) with large e: GLYZ 2015 Thm 3 (odd n>=50) and the 2016 Savchev-Chen 'shorter long' theorem both apply in C_p coordinates (n=p). The prior screen called them inapplicable, which is true only for n=2p. Nothing here is major. LS, LS+ and STAB in general, and ordered Olson for D_2p, remain OPEN.

findings.claim: Index-one theorem (classical import, proof not replayed). Proposition I-small step (B) uses it with n=p and BASE1 S4 with n=2p. The statement read matches the parent's import record.

findings.source: F. Chen (joint with S. Savchev), 'Shorter long minimal zero-sum sequences over finite cyclic groups', CANT 2016 Graz, slide p.4; [2]=Savchev-Chen DM 307 (2007), [4]=Yuan JCTA 114 (2007)

findings.claim: SC2007 already contains both normal-form steps of Proposition I-small. Thm 8 (index <1 for zero-free sequences longer than n/2) gives step (B). Prop 5 and Thm 7 ('behaving': every integer in [1,S] is a subset sum) give step (C): r>=(p+1)/2 terms with S<=p-1 is exactly Prop 5 with k=p. What I-small adds is (A), Lemma AP', and the CF-(L) contradiction, on top of lane scaffolding [INFERENCE for the identification].
findings.quote: Proposition 5 Let k be a positive integer. Each sequence with positive integer terms of length at least k/2 and sum less than k is behaving.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Long zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups, Discrete Math. 307 (2007) 2671-2679
findings.date_version: arXiv math/0602568v1, 2006-02-25; journal version not read
findings.verified: read; mapping to I-small steps is [INFERENCE]
findings.scope: Z_n zero-free sequences of length >n/2; applied with n=p to U

findings.claim: Classical inverse theorem for length 2n-3, re-derived in SC2008 from its Thm 5. Together with EGZ it gives LS(p,p-2) for every prime p>=5 (derivation in theorem_comparison) [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Now it is easy to infer that each n-zero-free sequence of length 2n−3, n > 4, is similar to 0^{n−1}1^{n−2} or 0^{n−1}1^{n−3}2.
findings.source: S. Savchev, F. Chen, Long n-zero-free sequences in finite cyclic groups, Discrete Math. 308 (2008) 1-8, Sec. 4 (credits Ordaz-Flores [9] for 2n-3)
findings.date_version: arXiv math/0604356v1, 2006-04-16; journal version not read
findings.scope: Z_n, n-term zero sums; 'similar' means affine maps including translations

findings.claim: Classical inverse theorem for length 2n-2 (Yuster-Peterson; Bialostocki-Dierker), as stated in SC2008. It handles the |Y|=3p-2 branch of the LS(p,p-2) shortcut.
findings.quote: These are the sequences containing exactly two distinct elements a and b of Z_n, each of them repeated n−1 times, such that a − b generates Z_n.
findings.source: SC2008 Sec. 1, restating T. Yuster, B. Peterson, Canad. J. Math. 36 (1984) 529-536 and A. Bialostocki, P. Dierker, Discrete Math. 110 (1992) 1-8
findings.read_scope: Sec. 1 and Sec. 4 (SC2008 re-derives it for n>2)

findings.claim: Range of SC2008 Thm 5 for the EGZ split. Apply it in C_p to X=Y-A, where A is a p-term x-zero-sum inside a long zero-sum. It gives a normal form iff |X|=2p-2e+1>3p/2-1, i.e. p>4e-4: p>=11 for e=3 and p>=13 for e=4, which contains both LS-small ranges. Similarity includes translations, which do not preserve the even-length window, so casework remains. Not executed [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: A sequence of length greater than 3n/2 − 1 in Z_n is n-zero-free if and only if it is similar to the union of two sequences α and β ... L(α) < n and L(1 − β) < n.
findings.verified: read; the range computation and route are [INFERENCE]
findings.scope: route for LS with e<p/4+1; also a possible route to LS+(p,p-2) (out of scope)

findings.claim: Where the route stops. SC2008's examples showing its range is optimal live in Z_p. They can therefore appear as C_p coordinates of odd sequences, so the EGZ-split normal form genuinely ends near e≈p/4+1. The prior screen dismissed these examples because they contain even elements, but that applies only to n=2p [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: There are n-zero-free sequences of length n − 1 + ⌊n/2⌋ that do not obey the conclusion of Theorem 5. Here are examples. For an odd n ≥ 9, consider the sequence 0^{n−1}2^{(n−5)/2}3^2.
findings.scope: limit of classical-normal-form routes for LS

findings.claim: A second published restatement of Ordaz-Flores, consistent with SC2008. Thm 3.1 gives a two-value normal form (u+v>=2p-2k+2) for p-zero-free sequences of length 2p-k with 2<=k<=[(p+1)/3]+1. For X=Y-A it applies when 2e-1<=[(p+1)/3]+1, a narrower range than SC2008. Tool only [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Suppose S is any sequence in Z_n of length 2n− 3 such that S has no zero-sum subsequence of length n. Then there exists a, b ∈ Z_n such that Z_n is generated by b − a
findings.source: W. D. Gao, A. Panigrahi, R. Thangadurai, Proc. Indian Acad. Sci. Math. Sci. 115 (2005) 67-77
findings.read_scope: pp. 67-74: intro, Thm 3.1 statement and proof, Lemma 2.4
findings.scope: Z_p, p-term zero sums; parity and window not treated

findings.claim: Zeng-Yuan 2011 applies to BASE1's T: length 2p+2=2*floor(2p/2)+2, and a factorization into two atoms follows from D(C_2p)=2p plus BASE1 S1-S2. This gives the index-2 normal form directly, bypassing S3's S1-sharp import and the index-one route in S4-S8. With elementary counting, BASE1's classification follows (theorem_comparison) [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: zero-sum sequence of length |S|≥2⌊n/2⌋+2. Suppose that S can be decomposed into a product of at most two minimal zero-sum sequences. Then there exists some g∈G such that S=(n1g)⋅…⋅(n|S|g), ... n1+n2+⋯+n|S|=2n.
findings.source: X. Zeng, P. Yuan, Indexes of long zero-sum sequences over cyclic groups, Eur. J. Combin. 32(8) (2011) 1213-1221, DOI 10.1016/j.ejc.2011.06.007
findings.read_scope: summary and reference list only (full text returned HTTP 403)

findings.claim: Tool for the open LS case (I) with large e. For odd n>=50 the theorem covers zero-sum-free sequences of length in (floor(n/3)+1, floor(n/2)]. It therefore applies in C_p coordinates (n=p>=53) to the zero-free part U when r<=p/2, exactly where the candidate notes that index-one is unavailable. The prior screen's 'inapplicable' holds only for n=2p [INFERENCE].
findings.quote: Let n ≥ 50 be an odd integer ... zero-sum free sequence of length ⌊n/3⌋ + 1 < |S| ≤ ⌊n/2⌋ ... by removing at most two elements ... index is not more than 1 − 4/n.
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Yuan, J. Zhuang, Arch. Math. 105 (2015) 361-370, Theorem 3
findings.date_version: author preprint dated 2015-05-07; journal version not read

findings.claim: A second tool for large e. The minimal zero-sum sequence U(-sigma(U)) with length in [floor(p/3)+3, floor(p/2)+1] has a 1-element or 2-element basis (n>=10). The slides call the source a manuscript; I did not check whether it was published.
findings.quote: Theorem 4. A sequence over the cyclic group Cn, n ≥ 10, with length in [⌊n/3⌋+3, ⌊n/2⌋+1] is a minimal zero-sum sequence if and only if it has a 1-element or a 2-element basis.

findings.claim: Zeng-Yuan 2023 treats the inverse problem for zero-sums of length at most h(S). That is a different invariant, and it implies neither LS-small nor BASE1.
findings.quote: It is interesting to study the corresponding inverse problem, that is to find information on the structure of the sequence S which does not contain zero-sum subsequences of length at most h(S).
findings.source: X. Zeng, P. Yuan, Electron. J. Combin. 30(4) (2023) #P4.21
findings.read_scope: abstract (pp. 1-12 read by the prior scout)

findings.claim: Recent length-restricted invariant, s_<=k (short lengths in rank >=2 and p-groups). It is not the window [2kappa+2,2p] on the odd coset, and it does not apply.
findings.quote: Denote by s_≤k(G) the smallest positive integer l ∈ N ∪ {+∞} such that each sequence of length l over G has a non-empty zero-sum subsequence of length at most k.
findings.source: K. Zhao, On zero-sum subsequences in a finite abelian group of length not exceeding a given number
findings.read_scope: abstract, Sec. 1 and part of Secs 2-3

findings.claim: Forbidden-length invariant disc_l, which forbids a single length. Different hypothesis; it does not apply.
findings.quote: For every positive integer ℓ, let disc_ℓ(G) be the smallest positive integer t such that each sequence S over G of length |S| ≥ t has a nonempty zero-sum subsequence of length not equal to ℓ.
findings.source: W. Gao, Y. Li, P. Zhao, J. Zhuang, Colloq. Math. 144 (2016) 31-44
findings.scope: abelian G incl. cyclic groups and C_2+C_2m

theorem_comparison.setting: Odd elements of C_2p correspond to (1,x) in C_2xC_p. A subsequence of length l is a zero-sum iff l is even and its x-sum is 0 mod p. (ZP_kappa) forbids x-zero-sums of even size in [2kappa+2,2p]. A long zero-sum is an x-zero-sum of even size >=2p+2.
candidate_statements: LS(p,kappa) (LS-scope-v1.md:10-12): |Y|>=p+2kappa+1 and (ZP_kappa) imply (S1_kappa). LS+ (LSplus-scope-v1.md:11): (ZP_kappa) and not (S1_kappa) imply |Y|<=3kappa+1.
LS-II' (proof-LS-caseII-v2-addendum-1.md:6-7, 25-26): for p>=7 and kappa0+1<=kappa<=p-2, every LS counterexample of threshold length is in case (I).

Corollary LS-small (proof-LS-caseI-smalldelta-v1.md:37-39): LS(p,p-2) for p>=7, LS(p,p-3) for p>=11, LS(p,p-4) for p>=13. The proof is Prop I-small: (B) index-one (line 17) and (C) every integer in [0,S] is a subset sum (line 20).

BASE1 and BASE1+ (proof-STAB-base-p1mod3-v1.md:13-15): p=1 mod 3, kappa=(2p+1)/3. Length 2p+2 with (ZP) and a long zero-sum forces E2 or E3, and every such Y has length <=2p+2. S3 (lines 26-28) imports S1-sharp and S4 (lines 29-32) uses index-one with n=2p.

classical_shortcuts.name: LS(p,p-2) via EGZ split [INFERENCE, unreviewed]
classical_shortcuts.statement: For every prime p>=5, an odd Y over C_2p with no zero-sum of length 2p-2 or 2p and |Y|>=3p-3 has no zero-sum of length >=2p+2.
classical_shortcuts.derivation: Applying EGZ twice gives |Y|<=3p-2. Let T be a long zero-sum. EGZ inside T gives a p-term x-zero-sum A of T. Then X:=Y-A has |X| in {2p-3,2p-2}. X has no p-term x-zero-sum (else a 2p zero-sum) and no (p-2)-term one (else 2p-2), and it contains T-A, an x-zero-sum of odd size. By the 2n-2 and 2n-3 theorems, X is w^(p-1)(w+d)^(p-2 or p-1) or w^(p-1)(w+d)^(p-3)(w+2d), with d!=0. The (p-2)-term sums are -2w+td for t in [0,p-2] in the first shape, which covers every residue except -2w+(p-1)d. In the second shape the possible t+2eps cover [0,p-1], so every residue occurs. So X avoids a (p-2)-term x-zero-sum only if X=w^(p-1)(-w)^(p-2 or p-1). In that case any x-zero-sum w^i(-w)^j has i=j and hence even size, contradicting the odd size of T-A.
classical_shortcuts.status: same cell as the candidate (plus p=5, which S1-sharp already covers). The proof is shorter and uses only classical imports.

classical_shortcuts.name: BASE1 Theorem via Zeng-Yuan 2011 [INFERENCE, unreviewed; ZY2011 read at summary level]
classical_shortcuts.statement: Same as BASE1, for p=1 mod 3 and p>=7.
classical_shortcuts.derivation: Y=T has length 2p+2. Since D(C_2p)=2p, T has a proper zero-sum. BASE1 S1-S2, which are elementary, show every proper zero-sum is minimal, so T is a product of two atoms. ZY2011 then gives T=prod(n_i g) with sum n_i=4p. The terms are odd, so g is an odd generator and every n_i is odd. Let y_i=(n_i-1)/2, N=the positive y_i, s=|N| and m=(p-4)/3, so sum_N y=p-1=3m+3. A proper zero-sum W satisfies sum_W n=2p, |W|=2p-2*sum_V and needs 2p-|V|-2*sum_V<=2p+2-s copies of g, where V=W∩N. Hence (ZP) holds iff every V in N with sum_V<=m has |V|+2*sum_V<=s-3. At most 3 elements are >=m+1, and exactly 3 forces N=(m+1)^3, which is E3. Otherwise there are b<=2 big elements and the small part has sum >m (otherwise V=small part gives 2*sum<=b-3). Take the ascending maximal prefix V with sum_V<=m and let y* be the next element. If y*=1, then b=0 and N=1^(p-1), which is E2. If y*>=2, the condition gives y*(2*sum_V+3-b)+sum_V<=sum_small; its left side is a concave quadratic in y*, positive at y*=2 and y*=m once m>=2, so no such y* exists. When m=1 no small element can be >=2.
classical_shortcuts.status: corollary-level given ZY2011. It does not need S1-sharp. BASE1+ still needs SLZ3 (lane-accepted).

theorem_comparison.stronger_shortcut_assessment: In coverage, nothing located is strictly stronger. The only candidate for something stronger is the unexecuted EGZ-split plus SC2008 route, which might give LS for every e<p/4+1 (a band kappa>3p/4-1). If it works it would strictly extend LS-small, but it is not established.

significance.rubric: Major would mean a new method, a solved prominent problem (ordered Olson for D_2p), or a published bound improved under matched assumptions. None is established.
significance.LS_p_minus_2: Immediate corollary of classical results [INFERENCE]. Credit it as routine. Not located verbatim in print.
significance.LS_p_minus_3_and_4: Priority unknown. Plausible specialist delta and possibly routine through SC2008 (not executed). The candidate's method is the SC2007 normal form plus an elementary AP lemma on lane scaffolding.
significance.LS_II_prime: Routine internal reduction. No standalone priority value.
significance.BASE1: Corollary-level given ZY2011 plus about 12 lines of counting [INFERENCE]. The E2/E3 statement was not located in print. Modest sharp inverse statement for a single cell family.
significance.BASE1_plus: Modest. Its novelty cannot be judged apart from SLZ3 and S1-sharp, which are unpublished lane results.
significance.overall: Not a major contribution. These are inputs to ordered Olson for D_2p, and LS, LS+ and STAB in general stay OPEN.

counterpoints: Both classical shortcuts are my own hand derivations and have not been reviewed. A hostile review should check them before any credit wording changes.

ZY2011 was read only as the zbMATH summary. If the full text adds hypotheses (for example on order-2 terms, or requiring g to be a generator), the BASE1 shortcut needs adjusting. BASE1's own route avoids ZY2011 by using S1-sharp and index-one.
'Routine' is not 'published'. In this screen no source states LS(p,p-2), the LS-small cells or the E2/E3 classification.
For e=3 and e=4 the SC2008 route depends on the translation parameter and on boundary cases where u or v is near p-1. A specialist could judge it routine or not; I did not decide.

Classical normal forms provably stop near e≈p/4+1 (the range-optimality examples of SC2007 and SC2008) and again near length floor(p/3)+2 (Chen-Savchev). LS for large e needs new input whichever route is used.
The e=2 shortcut does not by itself give STAB or LS+.
access_holes: Zeng-Yuan 2011 full text: the ScienceDirect PDF (bronze OA per OpenAlex, pii S0195669811001053) returned HTTP 403. Only the zbMATH summary was read; nothing was bypassed.

Ordaz-Flores (1995 Spanish homage volume, Bahía Blanca) is inaccessible. Yuster-Peterson 1984 and Bialostocki-Dierker 1992 primaries were not read. I used SC2008's re-derivation and the GPT2005 restatement.
SC2007 and SC2008 journal versions were not read; arXiv v1 was read in full. GLYZ: preprint only. Chen-Savchev 'shorter long': slides only.
The JNT 2026 paper 'zero-sum subsequences with length not divided by a given number' returned 403; I saw only its title and search snippet.
Forward citations were screened by title only (OpenAlex: 9 citers of ZY2011, 19 of SC2008). No CNKI, thesis or Google Scholar search was done.
unverified_or_dropped: [INFERENCE] the LS(p,p-2) derivation; the ZY2011 route to BASE1 and its counting argument; the p>4e-4 range comparison; the applicability of GLYZ and Chen-Savchev in C_p coordinates; the point that SC2008's optimality examples can occur at n=p.
Not executed: LS(p,p-3) and LS(p,p-4) through the SC2008 normal form.
